title: Recognition principle for S-families of broken lines
statement_scope: Whole Theorem 2.4.1: let pi: L_S -> S be a continuous map of topological spaces and mu: R x L_S -> L_S a continuous R-action stabilizing each fiber of pi. Then (pi, mu) is an S-family of broken lines in the sense of Definition 2.1.3 if and only if: (A1) for each s in S there exists a directed homeomorphism L_s ~= [0,1]; (A2) the restriction pi|L_S^R is unramified as in Definition 2.1.3; (A3) pi is closed; (A4) for x,y in L_S with pi(x)=pi(y), the set {(x,y) in L_S x_S L_S : x <=_{L_S} y} is closed in L_S x_S L_S; (A5) the restriction of pi to the non-fixed locus L_S^circ = L_S minus L_S^R has the local lifting property, namely every x in L_S^circ has a neighborhood U subset S of pi(x) and a continuous section sigma: U -> L_S^circ with sigma(pi(x))=x and pi sigma = id_U.

proof_spans.label: Proof of Theorem 2.4.1, converse, using Proposition 2.5.3

difficulty_reason: author-work-bearing-core-v1-20261114: H3 because Theorem 2.4.1 on author PDF pp.14-15 with its converse proof on p.18 is a research-bearing recognition principle. Necessity on p.15 derives (A1)-(A5) from a local directed product structure, compactness of [0,1] and the fixed-locus decomposition; the converse on p.18 uses I-sections (Proposition 2.5.3), translation distance and properness to build a directed closed bijection gamma: L_S -> [0,1]. This is a substantial author argument, not a routine definition check.

difficulty_evidence.bearing_core: Necessity converts a directed product structure into closedness, order-closedness and local lifting; converse builds a global directed homeomorphism gamma from I-sections and translation distance and proves it is a closed bijection.
